newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Nov industrial production.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Nov industrial production.

text.p: Following are economists' comments after the German Economics Ministry reported that pan-German industrial production rose by a seasonally-adjusted 1.6 percent in November from the previous month and by 1.3 percent year-on-year.

"The production rise was to be expected given the rise in orders in October. It doesn't change our forecast that German GDP rose 1.5 percent in 1996. We expect fourth-quarter GDP to be stagnant or slightly up. But I think we'll see production stagnating in the first quarter of 1997 due to the cold weather, increases in pension contributions and the ending of tax breaks in east Germany."

MICHAEL HOCHGUERTEL, BHF-BANK - "It is definitely a bit higher (than expected). It is not strong enough to bring a really heavy impact. It is only one of 12 numbers. We have low M3, high unemployment, low productivity and a reduced picture for GDP so I think the Bundesbank will come under pressure on the repo side."

ROB HAYWARD, BANK OF AMERICA - "Growth in the fourth quarter will be flat at best and there may even be a small contraction. If we are looking at any growth in the consumer side we can forget about it. The economy will remain weak, M3 will come into target range.

"I have a slightly negative Bund outlook for the first quarter. There is a lot of supply. Economic arguments favour the German market and we should see some outperformance. The spread (against T-Notes) could widen to 100 basis points."
